turnaround_reason: High-end bike demand collapsed (~42% segment decline) on post-COVID inventory digestion and weak discretionary spend, dragging FOXF from the $30s to the low teens. Q2 2026 marked an inflection: powersports surged and management raised the full-year outlook, signaling channel inventory has largely cleared.
bullish_points: Q2 2026 beat: EBITDA topped estimates by ~$5M and management LIFTED the 2026 sales view
Powersports (PVG) up 22.5% YoY in Q2, +28% in H1 as OEM channel inventory normalizes
Bike and aftermarket showing stabilization after a brutal downcycle
Clear margin-repair ramp guided: ~12.2% EBITDA in Q2 -> 13.6% Q3 -> ~15.6% Q4 as tariffs anniversary and cost programs hit full run-rate
$75M profit-recovery savings program targeted by FY2027
Marucci bat launch delayed into a stronger period is an incremental tailwind
bearish_points: TTM profit margin -20% reflects prior impairments/goodwill damage; still not GAAP-clean
Debt/equity ~102 leaves limited cushion if the consumer weakens again
Analyst mean target ~$21.8 sits right at the current price -- Street sees fair value, not deep upside
Bike recovery is 'stabilization' not growth; a discretionary re-slowdown would re-break the thesis
F-150 chassis supply constraints and tariffs remain swing factors on the margin ramp
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings confirming the guided margin step-up (13.6% EBITDA) and continued powersports strength
suggested_trade: Starter-to-medium spot position $20-22, add on a confirmed Q3 margin beat. Options fine for sizing but spot preferred given still-negative GAAP.
key_risk: A renewed pullback in discretionary consumer spend (bikes, powersports) stalls the volume recovery and the margin ramp misses.
would_skip_if: Q3 shows the margin ramp slipping or powersports growth decelerating sharply -- the whole thesis rests on the guided inflection being real.
